let \(\pi_k^v(o)\) be its prefix mass under this model, and define the rare-action-history factor from \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities} by
\[
\mathfrak a_k(o)
=
L^{-(Q-\ell)}
\prod_{i:\,k-\ell<i\le k}\mathbf 1\{a_i=1\},
\]
with the empty product equal to one. Then
\[
\sum_{o}\pi_k^v(o)\,\mathfrak a_k(o)^2
=
L^{-2(Q-\ell)}
\left(\frac{1}{L}\right)^{|\{i:\ k-\ell<i\le k\}|},
\]
where the sum ranges over all action/reward-symbol prefixes of length \(k\).

cb674d1068e5f5720bb152bda8056f474259881a.title: Terminal posterior window bound
cb674d1068e5f5720bb152bda8056f474259881a.body:
Let \(N,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\).  Put \(\alpha=\exp\{-(1/t_0)\}\).  In the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}, for an observed prefix \(o=((a_1,y_1),\ldots,(a_k,y_k))\), write
\[
\pi_v(o)
=
\frac{
\sum_{h\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}}
\mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\lambda_v(h;o)
}{
\mathsf M_v(o)
}.
\]
For \(d\in\mathbb N\), define the lower posterior window
\[
\Lambda_d(o)
=
\prod_{\substack{0\le i<k\\ k-d\le i}}
\left(1-c_0(t_0)\,\pi_v(o_{\le i})\right),
\]
where \(o_{\le i}\) is the prefix of \(o\) containing its first \(i\) action--reward pairs.

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive tilt.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(C>1\).
\item \textbf{(Mature window.)} \(Q\le k\).
\end{itemize}
Then the terminal-depth posterior satisfies
\[
\pi_v(o)
\le
\frac{\alpha^Q}{\Lambda_Q(o)}.
\]

2d66f8ec011821622905f617e21344faaebecbc1.title: Posterior window power bound
2d66f8ec011821622905f617e21344faaebecbc1.body:
Let \(N,Q,k,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C,b\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and let \(o=((a_0,y_0),\ldots,(a_{k-1},y_{k-1}))\) be an observed prefix for the signed-depth family of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  Write
\[
c_0(t_0)=\frac{1-\alpha(t_0)}{4},
\]
and, for \(0\le m\le k\), write \(o_{\le m}\) for the first \(m\) observed pairs.  For any observed prefix \(o'\), define the raw terminal-depth posterior by
\[
\pi_v(o')
=
\frac{\sum_h \mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\lambda_v(h;o')}
     {\sum_h \lambda_v(h;o')}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative amplitude.)} \(0\le c_0(t_0)\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative base.)} \(0\le 1-c_0(t_0)b\).
\item \textbf{(Window length.)} \(d\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Strict-prefix posterior bound.)} For every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\),
\[
\pi_v(o_{\le i})\le b.
\]
\end{itemize}
Define the final \(d\)-prefix lower window by
\[
\Lambda_d(o)
=
\prod_{\substack{0\le i<k\\ k-d\le i}}
\left(1-c_0(t_0)\pi_v(o_{\le i})\right).
\]
Then
\[
\bigl(1-c_0(t_0)b\bigr)^d\le \Lambda_d(o).
\]

5dd3ad54f5a6edcfbdda88eeb83382cfd9c8db40.title: Crude terminal posterior bound
5dd3ad54f5a6edcfbdda88eeb83382cfd9c8db40.body:
Let \(N,Q,k\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive temperature.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive log-overlap.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
For the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}, write
\[
\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0),
\qquad
c_0=\frac{1-\alpha}{4}.
\]
For every observed prefix \(o\in(\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\})^k\), define the raw terminal-depth posterior by
\[
\pi_v(o)
=
\frac{
\sum_h \mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\,\lambda_v(h;o)
}{
\mathsf M_v(o)
},
\qquad
\mathsf M_v(o)=\sum_h \lambda_v(h;o),
\]
where the sums range over the signed-depth hidden states at depth horizon \(Q\). Then
\[
\pi_v(o)
\le
\left(\frac{\alpha}{1-c_0}\right)^Q .
\]

dc2040cdba5062deba1d9e9c57c31fe889ab928f.title: Initial-window posterior bound
dc2040cdba5062deba1d9e9c57c31fe889ab928f.body:
Let \(N,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let \(k\in\mathbb N\), and let
\[
o:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to \{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}
\]
be an observed action/reward prefix for the signed-depth construction of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  Write \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\).  For any prefix \(o'\), define the raw terminal-depth posterior by
\[
\pi_v(o')
=
\frac{\sum_{h:\,J(h)=Q}\lambda_v(h;o')}
     {\sum_h \lambda_v(h;o')}.
\]
Define the initial lower posterior window over the available prefixes by
\[
\Lambda_k(o)
=
\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}
\left(1-c_0\,\pi_v(o_{\le i})\right),
\]
where \(o_{\le i}\) is the prefix of \(o\) of length \(i\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Nontrivial overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\item \textbf{(Initial window.)} \(k<Q\).
\end{itemize}
Then the terminal-depth posterior after observing \(o\) satisfies
\[
\pi_v(o)\le \frac{\alpha^Q}{\Lambda_k(o)}.
\]

f74e41e4fc052d5c5ee41aa56bef9c395234af22.title: Terminal prefix mass identity
f74e41e4fc052d5c5ee41aa56bef9c395234af22.body:
Let \(U,k,Q\in\mathbb N\) with \(U\ge 1\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and consider the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} at horizon \(U+k\).  For an action/reward-symbol prefix \(o\) of length \(k\), define the joint prefix-and-terminal-depth mass at the cut after the first \(k\) epochs by
\[
m_v^Q(o)
=
\Pr_v\{(A_1,R_1),\ldots,(A_k,R_k)=o,\ J_{k+1}=Q\}.
\]
For each hidden coordinate \(h\in\{0,\ldots,2(Q+1)-1\}\), let \(J(h)=\lfloor h/2\rfloor\), and let \(\lambda_v(h;o)\) be the unnormalized filter mass, as in \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities}, assigned after observing \(o\) to the cut state with hidden coordinate \(h\).  Then
\[
m_v^Q(o)
=
\sum_{h=0}^{2(Q+1)-1}
\mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\,\lambda_v(h;o).
\]

ea2ad0836c8172265ed5d099e63945f0bbe9f98e.title: Next reward numerator
ea2ad0836c8172265ed5d099e63945f0bbe9f98e.body:
Let \(U,k,N,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and consider the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} with horizon \(N\), terminal depth \(Q\), initial weights \(p_v\), behavior policy \(b\), and reward-symbol/hidden-state kernel \(K_v\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive time scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive behavior perturbation.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
Write
\[
c_0(t_0)=\frac{1-\alpha}{4},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is the signed-depth mixing parameter, and write \(\phi(0)=-1\), \(\phi(1)=1\).  For any observed action/reward-symbol prefix \(o\in(\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\})^k\), let
\[
\lambda_v(h;o)
\]
denote the unnormalized signed-depth filter mass, after the prefix \(o\), assigned to observed state \(0\) and packed hidden state \(h\in\{0,\ldots,2(Q+1)-1\}\).  Decode the packed hidden state by
\[
J(h)=\bigl\lfloor h/2\bigr\rfloor,
\qquad
U(h)=
\begin{cases}
+1, & h \equiv 1 \pmod 2,\\
-1, & h \equiv 0 \pmod 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{\tau}
\mathbf 1\!\left\{ ((a_i,r_i))_{i=1}^k(\tau)=o\right\}
\,\omega_v(\tau)\,\phi\!\left(r_{k+1}(\tau)\right)
=
v\,c_0(t_0)
\sum_{h=0}^{2(Q+1)-1}
\mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\,U(h)\,\lambda_v(h;o),
\]
where the outer sum is over all finite signed-depth trajectories \(\tau\) of horizon \(U+k+1\), and \(\omega_v(\tau)\) is their chronological path weight under \(p_v\), \(b\), and \(K_v\).

fe3c3b06047652534c4623de438e88772e66f8f0.title: Singleton pair target value
fe3c3b06047652534c4623de438e88772e66f8f0.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(v\in\{0,1\}\), and write
\[
\sigma(v)=
\begin{cases}
+1, & v=1,\\
-1, & v=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\[
\eta_T=\frac{1}{4\sqrt T},
\]
with the usual real-valued convention that this expression is \(0\) when \(T=0\). Suppose the scalar parameters satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Initial scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap scale.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radius scale.)} \(C\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(M_T^v\) be the singleton-state finite experiment with one observed state and one hidden state, fair behavior and target policies \(b(a\mid x_\star)=e(a\mid x_\star)=1/2\), reward support \(\{-1,+1\}\), and reward-transition kernel that assigns, from every state-action pair, probability
\[
\frac{1+\sigma(v)y\eta_T}{2}
\]
to reward \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\) and next state \((x_\star,h_\star)\). Then the stationary target-policy mean reward of \cref{obj:def:target-value} satisfies
\[
\theta(K,e;M_T^v)=\sigma(v)\eta_T .
\]

b4d2f3a210b3128d5cbd13ee80c3661e69b5fe46.title: Observed KL budget
b4d2f3a210b3128d5cbd13ee80c3661e69b5fe46.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(T\ge 1\), and set \(\eta_T=1/(4\sqrt T)\). Let \(M_T^{-}\) and \(M_T^{+}\) be the two finite singleton-state experiments with one observed state \(x_\star\), one hidden state, initial mass at the single joint state, fair behavior and target policies \(b=e\) on \(\{0,1\}\), and reward code \(\mathsf r\in\{0,1\}\) decoded as \(2\mathsf r-1\). Under \(M_T^\sigma\), for \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), the reward-transition kernel returns to the single joint state and assigns reward \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\) probability
\[
\frac{1+\sigma y\eta_T}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P^{\mathrm{obs}}_{M_T^\sigma}\) for the image of the decoded trajectory law under the observed-path projection, the required KL budget holds in the direction
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
\mathbb P^{\mathrm{obs}}_{M_T^-}
\,\middle\|\,
\mathbb P^{\mathrm{obs}}_{M_T^+}
\right)
\le \frac14 .
\]

d902d9f8fc2ebaaa5ddcd6eef69757288e949b19.title: Two-point risk floor
d902d9f8fc2ebaaa5ddcd6eef69757288e949b19.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M_0,M_1\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  After identifying their common observed alphabet, write \(\mathbb P_j\) for the observed-data law of \(M_j\) and \(\theta_j\) for the target value of \(M_j\) from \cref{obj:def:target-value}, \(j\in\{0,1\}\).  Let \(s\) be a nonnegative separation radius and let \(\chi\) be a nonnegative KL upper bound.  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Common observable structure.)} The two models have the same observed-alphabet cardinality, the same behavior policy, and the same target policy.
\item \textbf{(Information bound.)} \(\mathbb P_0\ll\mathbb P_1\),
\[
\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)\le \chi,
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)<\infty .
\]
\item \textbf{(Target separation.)}
\[
2s\le |\theta_0-\theta_1| .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then every raw observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), viewed as a real-valued measurable function of the observed-alphabet size, the policy pair, and the observed path, with \((\widehat\theta-\theta_j)^2\) integrable under \(\mathbb P_j\) at \(M_j\) for \(j=0,1\), satisfies
\[
\frac{s^2\exp(-\chi)}{4}
\le
\max\left\{
\mathbb E_{M_0}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)^2\right],
\mathbb E_{M_1}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_1)^2\right]
\right\}.
\]
Consequently, the minimax squared-error risk of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\frac{s^2\exp(-\chi)}{4}
\le
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C).
\]

ba1c1454c33ef23fd76821b98bc2d46530728161.title: Observed signed-depth law
ba1c1454c33ef23fd76821b98bc2d46530728161.body:
For \(T,Q\in\mathbb N\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and two-point alternative index \(v\), define
\[
\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}
\]
to be the observed-path law obtained by applying the observed-coordinate projection to the trajectory law of the embedded finite signed-depth model with horizon \(T\), parameters \((t_0,\zeta,C,Q)\), and alternative index \(v\).

9614f6dc73dca540c14e588dca34d324ceda77dd.title: Parametric pair target value
9614f6dc73dca540c14e588dca34d324ceda77dd.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(v\in\{0,1\}\), and define the sign
\[
\sigma(v)=
\begin{cases}
+1, & v=1,\\
-1, & v=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Put
\[
\eta_T=\frac{1}{4\sqrt T},
\]
with value \(0\) when \(T=0\). Suppose the scalar parameters satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Initial scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap scale.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radius scale.)} \(C\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(M_T^v\) be the singleton-state finite experiment with one observed state and one hidden state, fair behavior and target policies \(b(a\mid x_\star)=e(a\mid x_\star)=1/2\), reward support \(\{-1,+1\}\), and reward-transition kernel that assigns, from every state-action pair, probability
\[
\frac{1+\sigma(v)y\eta_T}{2}
\]
to reward \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\) and next state \((x_\star,h_\star)\). Then the stationary target-policy mean reward of \cref{obj:def:target-value}, evaluated in this experiment, satisfies
\[
\theta(K_{M_T^v},e_{M_T^v})=\sigma(v)\eta_T .
\]

6c4c21748295e2849956a837ffb02bbead16eb5e.title: Observed risk bound
6c4c21748295e2849956a837ffb02bbead16eb5e.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\) and let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\). Let \(\widehat\theta\) be an observable-data estimator of the admissible class used in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}: for each observed-alphabet size and policy pair, \(\widehat\theta\) is a measurable real-valued function of the observed path taking values in \([-1,1]\). For every
\[
M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in \mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\]
as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with \(\widehat\theta\) evaluated at the observed-alphabet size and policies of \(M\), the squared risk for the target value \(\theta(K,e)\) of \cref{obj:def:target-value} satisfies
\[
E_M\bigl[(\widehat\theta-\theta(K,e))^2\bigr]\le 4 .
\]

fc15ce895f2c0fabae122ecbac9e40366f85f68a.title: Target value range
fc15ce895f2c0fabae122ecbac9e40366f85f68a.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let
\(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in
\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) be a model in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Then the stationary target-policy mean reward \(\theta(K,e)\) of \cref{obj:def:target-value} lies in the unit interval:
\[
\theta(K,e)\in[-1,1].
\]

9960f258f89633d1b4e6b642e6747d6127e1076a.title: Target value is bounded
9960f258f89633d1b4e6b642e6747d6127e1076a.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let
\(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in

\(\cref{obj:ass:stationary-start,obj:ass:sequential-ignorability,obj:ass:pomdp-kernel,obj:ass:bounded-reward,obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap,obj:ass:policy-overlap}\). Then the stationary target-policy mean reward \(\theta(K,e)\) of \cref{obj:def:target-value} lies in the unit interval:
\[
\theta(K,e)\in[-1,1].
\]

groups.title: Behavior and target stationary joint-state laws
groups.body:
For a memoryless policy \(p\in\{b,e\}\), let \(P_p\) be the policy-induced Markov kernel on the joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\). Define \(d_p\in\Delta(\mathcal S)\) to be the stationary joint-state law satisfying
\[
d_pP_p=d_p .
\]
We write \(d_b\) for the behavior-policy stationary joint-state law and \(d_e\) for the target-policy stationary joint-state law.

groups.title: Unclipped partial-history average
groups.body:
For the balanced history depth \(k_T\), define the unclipped partial-history average by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\rm raw}_{k_T}
:=
\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^{T} Z_t(k_T),
\qquad
Z_t(k_T):=
Y_t\prod_{j=t-k_T}^{t}\rho_j .
\]
Here \(\rho_j=e(A_j\mid X_j)/b(A_j\mid X_j)\) on behavior-supported cells, with the zero-cell convention used for \(\rho_j\).

groups.title: Model-class assumption predicates
groups.body:
For an observable-data POMDP experiment \((\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\) with \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), policy-induced kernels \(P_p\), stationary laws \(d_p\), \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\), and \(L=\exp(\zeta)\), write
\[
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{pomdp}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{ign}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{start}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{reward}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{act}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{mix}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{stat}}
\]
for the following seven restrictions, respectively:
\[
\mathcal L(Y_t,X_{t+1},H_{t+1}\mid X_{1:t},H_{1:t},A_{1:t},Y_{1:t-1})
=
K(\cdot\mid X_t,H_t,A_t),
\qquad t=1,\ldots,T,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel};
\[
\Pr(A_t=a\mid X_{1:t},H_{1:t},A_{1:t-1},Y_{1:t-1})
=
b(a\mid X_t),
\qquad (a,t)\in\mathcal A\times\{1,\ldots,T\},
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability};
\[
S_1\sim d_b,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:stationary-start};
\[
\Pr(|Y_t|\le1)=1,
\qquad t=1,\ldots,T,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-reward};
\[
e(a\mid x)\le L b(a\mid x),
\qquad (a,x)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal X,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap};
\[
\|\nu P_p-\nu'P_p\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\alpha\|\nu-\nu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}},
\qquad (p,\nu,\nu')\in\{b,e\}\times\Delta(\mathcal S)^2,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:uniform-contraction}; and
\[
d_e(s)\le C d_b(s),
\qquad s\in\mathcal S,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap}.

groups.title: Observable laws and estimator-specific risk
groups.body:
For an experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), let \(\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M\) denote the probability law of the observed trajectory
\[
\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^T
\]
induced by \(M\) under the behavior policy \(b\). For any observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), define its estimator-specific worst-case squared risk over \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) by
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta)
:=
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_{\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M}
\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\theta(n_X,b,e,\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K,e)\right\}^2
\right],
\]
where \(n_X=|\mathcal X|\) is the revealed observed-alphabet size of \(M\). In particular,
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta_{k_T})
\]
is the preceding quantity evaluated at the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator from \(\cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}\) with the balanced history depth \(k_T\) from \(\cref{obj:def:history-depth}\).

groups.title: Target value of an indexed model
groups.body:
For an indexed model \(m\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), write \(K_m\) and \(e_m\) for its joint reward-transition kernel and target policy. The target value of \(m\) is
\[
\theta_m:=\theta(K_m,e_m),
\]
with \(\theta(K,e)\) the stationary target-policy causal value from \(\cref{obj:def:target-value}\).

groups.title: Observed-trajectory law
groups.body:
For a raw POMDP experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\), let
\[
\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M
\]
denote the probability law of the observed trajectory
\[
\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^{T}
\]
induced by the behavior-policy experiment \(M\). Equivalently, under \(\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(S_1\sim d_b\), \(A_t\sim b(\cdot\mid X_t)\), and \(K\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), with only \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)_{t=1}^{T}\) retained.

groups.title: Finite signed-depth observed-word law
groups.body:
For \(C>1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let
\[
\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{fin},T}
\]
be the finite observed-word law through horizon \(T\) generated by the signed-depth construction of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}. Its observed state is constant, its latent state is \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}\), its behavior and target policies satisfy \(b(1)=1/L\) and \(e(1)=1\), and its reward alphabet is \(\{-1,+1\}\) with
\[
\Pr_v(Y_t=y\mid J_t,U_t,A_t)
=
\frac{1+yvc_0U_t\mathbf 1\{J_t=Q\}}{2}.
\]
The initial latent law is \(d_b(j,u)=w_j(1+u\varepsilon_C L^{-j})/2\), and the resulting finite observation consists of the action-reward word \((A_t,Y_t)_{t=1}^{T}\), equivalently the finite observed trajectory with constant observed-state coordinate.

groups.title: Full trajectory law and observation map
groups.body:
For a raw POMDP experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\) with joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\), let \(\mathbb P_M\) denote the full behavior-policy trajectory law on
\[
(S_1,A_1,Y_1,S_2,\ldots,A_T,Y_T,S_{T+1}).
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_M\), the initial state satisfies \(S_1\sim d_b\), each action is drawn as \(A_t\sim b(\cdot\mid X_t)\), and the kernel \(K\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).

Let \(O\) be the observation map from a full trajectory to its observed trajectory,
\[
O(S_1,A_1,Y_1,\ldots,A_T,Y_T,S_{T+1})
:=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^{T},
\]
where \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\). The observed behavior-policy law is the pushforward
\[
\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\mathbb P_M\circ O^{-1}.
\]

synth_1.title: Memoryless binary policy carrier
synth_1.body:
For \(n_X\in\mathbb N\), a memoryless policy on an observed-state alphabet of size \(n_X\) is a function
\[
p:\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to\mathbb R .
\]
When the action alphabet is written as \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), we identify \(\mathrm{false}\) with \(0\) and \(\mathrm{true}\) with \(1\). This is a carrier only: no nonnegativity and no normalization is imposed here. The probability-vector restrictions on the behavior and target carriers are imposed later, on \(b\) in \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability} and on \(e\) in \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap}.

synth_2.title: Joint-state alphabet
synth_2.body:
For natural numbers \(n_X\) and \(n_H\), the finite observed--latent joint-state alphabet is
\[
\mathcal S(n_X,n_H)
:=
\{i\in\mathbb N: 0\le i<n_X\}
\times
\{j\in\mathbb N: 0\le j<n_H\}.
\]

synth_3.title: Full finite trajectory
synth_3.body:
For natural numbers \(T,n_X,n_H\), a full trajectory of length \(T\) is a pair
\[
\bigl((S_t)_{t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}},((A_t,Y_t))_{t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}}\bigr)
\in
\bigl(\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times \{0,\ldots,n_H-1\}\bigr)^{\{0,\ldots,T\}}
\times
\bigl(\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\times \mathbb R\bigr)^{\{0,\ldots,T-1\}} .
\]
Here \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\) is the observed--latent joint state at state time \(t\), with observed coordinate \(X_t\in\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\) and latent coordinate \(H_t\in\{0,\ldots,n_H-1\}\). At transition time \(t\), \(A_t\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\) is the Boolean action and \(Y_t\in\mathbb R\) is the reward; when actions are written numerically, \(\mathrm{false}\) is identified with \(0\) and \(\mathrm{true}\) with \(1\).

synth_4.title: Policy transition operator
synth_4.body:
For a raw experiment \(M\) with one-step kernel \(K\), a memoryless policy \(p\), and joint states \(s=(x,h)\) and \(s'\), define the policy-induced transition operator \(P_p\) by
\[
P_p(s,s')
:=
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}
p(a\mid x)\,
K\bigl(\{(r,\widetilde s): \widetilde s=s'\}\mid s,a\bigr).
\]

synth_5.title: Target reward regression
synth_5.body:
For any raw finite-state experiment \(M\) with target policy \(e\) and one-step law \(K\), and for every joint state \(s=(x,h)\in \{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n_H-1\}\), define the target-policy reward regression \(g_e\) by
\[
g_e(s)
=
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} e(a\mid x)\int r\,K(d r,d s'\mid s,a).
\]

synth_6.title: One-step policy ratio
synth_6.body:
For behavior and target policy functions \(b,e : \{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R\), the observable one-step policy ratio is
\[
\rho_t
=
\begin{cases}
0, & b(X_t,A_t)=0,\\
e(X_t,A_t)/b(X_t,A_t), & b(X_t,A_t)\ne 0.
\end{cases}
\]

synth_7.title: Derived contraction factor
synth_7.body:
For any real \(t_0\), define the contraction parameter \(\alpha\) by
\[
\alpha := \exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{t_0}\right).
\]

synth_8.title: Policy-overlap factor
synth_8.body:
For a real parameter \(\zeta\), define the policy-overlap constant \(L\) by
\[
L(\zeta)=\exp(\zeta).
\]

synth_9.title: Behavior and target stationary joint-state laws
synth_9.body:
For a memoryless policy \(p\in\{b,e\}\), let \(P_p\) be the policy-induced Markov kernel on the joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\). Define \(d_p\in\Delta(\mathcal S)\) to be the stationary joint-state law satisfying
\[
d_pP_p=d_p .
\]
We write \(d_b\) for the behavior-policy stationary joint-state law and \(d_e\) for the target-policy stationary joint-state law.

synth_10.title: Unclipped partial-history average
synth_10.body:
For the balanced history depth \(k_T\), define the unclipped partial-history average by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\rm raw}_{k_T}
:=
\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T}^{T-1} Z_t(k_T),
\qquad
Z_t(k_T):=
Y_t\prod_{j=t-k_T}^{t}\rho_j .
\]
Here \(\rho_j=e(A_j\mid X_j)/b(A_j\mid X_j)\) on behavior-supported cells, with the zero-cell convention used for \(\rho_j\).

synth_11.title: Model-class assumption predicates
synth_11.body:
For an observable-data POMDP experiment \((\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\) with \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), policy-induced kernels \(P_p\), stationary laws \(d_p\), \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\), and \(L=\exp(\zeta)\), write
\[
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{pomdp}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{ign}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{start}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{reward}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{act}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{mix}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{stat}}
\]
for the following seven restrictions, respectively:
\[
\mathcal L(Y_t,X_{t+1},H_{t+1}\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t},Y_{0:t-1})
=
K(\cdot\mid X_t,H_t,A_t),
\qquad t=0,\ldots,T-1,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel};
\[
\Pr(A_t=a\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t-1},Y_{0:t-1})
=
b(a\mid X_t),
\qquad (a,t)\in\mathcal A\times\{0,\ldots,T-1\},
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability};
\[
S_0\sim d_b,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:stationary-start};
\[
\Pr(|Y_t|\le1)=1,
\qquad t=0,\ldots,T-1,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-reward};
\[
e(a\mid x)\le L b(a\mid x),
\qquad (a,x)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal X,
\qquad e\text{ a probability vector at each }x,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap};
\[
\|\nu P_p-\nu'P_p\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\alpha\|\nu-\nu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}},
\qquad (p,\nu,\nu')\in\{b,e\}\times\Delta(\mathcal S)^2,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:uniform-contraction}; and
\[
d_e(s)\le C d_b(s),
\qquad s\in\mathcal S,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap}.

synth_12.title: Observable trajectory space
synth_12.body:
For a horizon \(T\) and observed-state cardinality \(n_X\), define the observable trajectory space \(\mathsf O_T\) by
\[
\mathsf O_T
=
\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\to
\bigl(\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R\bigr).
\]
Thus an element of \(\mathsf O_T\) records, at each epoch \(t<T\), the observed coordinate \(X_t\), the binary action \(A_t\), and the real reward \(Y_t\). Equivalently, it is the sequence \(((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1}\).

synth_13.title: Estimator-specific risk
synth_13.body:
Let
\[
M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))
\in \mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\]
be a model in the latent-overlap class of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, whose observed trajectory is
\[
\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1},
\]
and let \(\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M\) denote the probability law of \(\mathsf O_T\) induced by \(M\) under the behavior policy \(b\).

For any observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), its estimator-specific worst-case squared risk over \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta)
:=
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_{\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M}
\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\theta(n_X,b,e,\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K,e)\right\}^2
\right],
\]
where \(n_X=|\mathcal X|\) is the revealed observed-alphabet size of \(M\). In particular,
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta_{k_T})
\]
is this quantity evaluated at the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator \(\widehat\theta_{k_T}\) with balanced history depth \(k_T\).

synth_14.title: Target value of an indexed model
synth_14.body:
For an indexed model \(m\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), write \(K_m\) and \(e_m\) for its joint reward-transition kernel and target policy. The target value of \(m\) is
\[
\theta_m:=\theta(K_m,e_m),
\]
with \(\theta(K,e)\) the stationary target-policy causal value from \(\cref{obj:def:target-value}\).

synth_15.title: Observed-trajectory law
synth_15.body:
For a raw POMDP experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\), let
\[
\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M
\]
denote the probability law of the observed trajectory
\[
\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1}
\]
induced by the behavior-policy experiment \(M\). Equivalently, under \(\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(S_0\sim d_b\), \(A_t\sim b(\cdot\mid X_t)\), and \(K\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), with only \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)_{t=0}^{T-1}\) retained.

synth_16.title: Finite signed-depth observed-word law
synth_16.body:
For \(C>1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let
\[
\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{fin},T}
\]
be the finite observed-word law through horizon \(T\) generated by the signed-depth construction of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}. Its observed state is constant, its latent state is \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}\), its behavior and target policies satisfy \(b(1)=1/L\) and \(e(1)=1\), and its reward alphabet is \(\{-1,+1\}\) with
\[
\Pr_v(Y_t=y\mid J_t,U_t,A_t)
=
\frac{1+yvc_0U_t\mathbf 1\{J_t=Q\}}{2}.
\]
The initial latent law is \(d_b(j,u)=w_j(1+u\varepsilon_C L^{-j})/2\), and the resulting finite observation consists of the action-reward word \((A_t,Y_t)_{t=0}^{T-1}\), equivalently the finite observed trajectory with constant observed-state coordinate.

synth_17.title: Full trajectory law and observation map
synth_17.body:
For a raw POMDP experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\) with joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\), let \(\mathbb P_M\) denote the full behavior-policy trajectory law on
\[
(S_0,A_0,Y_0,S_1,\ldots,A_{T-1},Y_{T-1},S_T).
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_M\), the initial state satisfies \(S_0\sim d_b\), each action is drawn as \(A_t\sim b(\cdot\mid X_t)\), and the kernel \(K\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\).

Let \(O\) be the observation map from a full trajectory to its observed trajectory,
\[
O(S_0,A_0,Y_0,\ldots,A_{T-1},Y_{T-1},S_T)
:=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1},
\]
where \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\). The observed behavior-policy law is the pushforward
\[
\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\mathbb P_M\circ O^{-1}.
\]

synth_18.title: Observed signed-depth law
synth_18.body:
For \(T,Q\in\mathbb N\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and two-point alternative index \(v\), define
\[
\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}
\]
to be the observed-path law obtained by applying the observed-coordinate projection to the trajectory law of the embedded finite signed-depth model with horizon \(T\), parameters \((t_0,\zeta,C,Q)\), and alternative index \(v\).
